thread:
alert-bot: ALERT: SYNTHETIC_PROBE_FAILURE spike detected
alert-bot: probes: synthetic-canary-main (eu-west-1, us-west-2) — 42 failures in 5m (alert threshold: >5 failures / 1m). Severity: P2. Pager: #eng-oncall.

maya: ack — I'm on it. pinging infra and checking dashboards.

jordan: I don't see user-facing 5xx increase in last 10m, but embedding request latency pct99 is up ~120ms in eu-west-1.

liam: looking at the probe logs now — a lot of the failures are 429s from the embeddings service (rate-limit). the probe retries are tight (every 15s) so it's amplifying transient throttles.

maya: ok. immediate mitigation plan: 1) apply short suppression to the synthetic alert for affected regions (30m) to stop noisy pages, 2) change probe frequency to reduce amplification (15s -> 60s) and add exponential backoff in probe client, 3) raise the alert threshold while we investigate (5 -> 12 failures / 5m).

jordan: +1. will open a dashboard panel to show probe failure vs backend 429 rate side by side.

sam: no inbound customer reports yet, but I'm watching the support queue. will update if anything pops. :mag:

maya: executing step 1 now — applying suppression window. @alert-bot please confirm when suppression is active.

alert-bot: Suppression applied to alert SYNTHETIC_PROBE_FAILURE for 30m (regions: eu-west-1, us-west-2). Notifications silenced for the suppressed alert.

liam: prepping the probe config change, pushing a quick patch to the synthetic repo. snippet:
```yaml
# synthetic probe config (patched)
probes:
  - name: synthetic-canary-main
    regions: [eu-west-1, us-west-2]
    frequency_seconds: 60   # was 15
    retry_policy:
      enabled: true
      backoff: exponential
      initial_delay_ms: 200
      max_delay_ms: 5000
    failure_threshold: 3
```

maya: note the `failure_threshold` in probe config is per-probe. the alert rule is separate — we'll adjust that too.

liam: pushed change to branch `synth/temporal-backoff`. deploying to staging now, will roll to prod after smoke. commands I ran: `git push && ci deploy synthetic --env=prod --canary=2`

jordan: dashboard quick query (datadog/promql equivalent):
```
# failure rate for synthetic probe
sum(rate(synthetic_probe_failures_total{probe="synthetic-canary-main"}[5m])) by (region)

# backend 429 rate
sum(rate(embeddings_http_responses_total{code="429"}[5m])) by (region)
```

liam: staging looks good. no new failures in the canary run (15m). rolling prod now.

maya: changing alert definition temporarily:
- old: failures > 5 / 1m
- temp: failures > 12 / 5m (regions: eu-west-1, us-west-2)

jordan: added a dashboard panel `synth vs 429` and a notebook with the runbook steps. link: https://dashboards.internal/synth-429-correlation (will add to ticket).

sam: customer update: none so far; I'll stand by for any support hits and will text the escalation channel if customers report degraded experience.

maya: handing off to @liam for monitoring during the suppression window — I'll remain available until 22:00 UTC but switching to standby. liam, take it? :handshake:

liam: taking it. I'll watch error rates and will revert the suppression/thresholds if backend 429s subside or if user-facing errors increase. will create follow-up postmortem ticket with remediation items.

maya: follow-ups (post-incident):
- add jitter and exponential backoff by default to all synthetic probes
- tune probe sensitivity per-region based on backend throttling patterns (avoid global thresholds)
- create alert runbook section for probe-induced noise and a gating checklist before muting alerts
- add dashboard alert that correlates probe failures with backend 429/ratelimit spikes

jordan: created ticket INF-4237 and assigned to eng-infra + eng-runtime for next-week work. added links to dashboard and deploy logs.

alert-bot: NOTE: suppression window ends at 2019001800 (30m). Reminder will be posted 5m before expiration.

sam: thanks team. I'll update support playbook to include a single-sentence status note in case customers ask.

liam: will post a short incident summary to #incidents after we confirm stability. proceeding to monitor.

maya: thanks all. good triage, low customer impact so far. please include config diffs in the postmortem and assign follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
